“The current bittersweet backward glance, as directed by Trip Cullman and choreographed by Ellenore Scott, is so keen-eyed that it instantly qualifies as a rediscovery to reckon with.
The staging of Harry's soapy, multiplying betrayals is brisk and beautiful to watch.
No, we’ll probably never see I Can Get It for You Wholesale again after this, and certainly not with a cast like the one Cullman has assembled.
The story still feels a little tired, and so does the message.
That Wholesale ties itself to Jewish families also serves as an obstacle for a more coherent show.
Even with some of the greatest actors available, the material feels unremarkable.
A crosscurrent of compelling themes run fast and deep in the turbulent, terrific revival of I Can Get It For You Wholesale.
Director Trip Cullman has assembled an astonishing cast that does a remarkable job at every turn...
Quibbles aside, I Can Get It for You Wholesale is a show whose time, one hopes, has finally arrived.

Yes, Wholesale has its moments. But on the whole it remains a show with some contradictory messaging, particularly when it comes to building sympathy for a long-suffering Jewish community tarred with stereotypes and mistruths and conspiracies that a character like Harry Bogin only seems to reinforce.
The music is plentiful but there's very little to remember because Harold Rome's music is unremarkable.
